title: Console has no way to connect the Papyrus CLI or a reporting agent to a site
description:
A person working with a reporting agent has to know, from outside the product, that the agent needs a CLI sign-in and which command does it. Found 2026-11-03 starting a Machines on Machines Story with a reporting agent: the agent could not work until Ryan ran a sign-in command the agent had to tell him about. No console page mentions papyrus login, login --remote or the site's public login file.

Goal: from the signed-in newsroom console, someone can connect the CLI or an agent to this site without reading the docs or asking anyone.

Design questions for the UX pass:
- Where it lives (app/newsroom/settings is the obvious candidate) and whether a Story's reporting view also links to it, since that is where the need shows up.
- The per-site command with a copy button, filled in from the site's own origin, so nobody types a host name.
- Local versus remote: papyrus login <site> on a machine with a browser, papyrus login --remote for an agent with none, where the person approves on their phone. Only offer remote on sites with cliRemoteLogin on.
- Prose for an editor who does not use a terminal: what connecting an agent lets it do, and that it acts as them.
- Whether to show this person's active CLI sign-ins and let them end one. Follow-up unless the backend already exposes it.

Rules: Lucide icons, flat fills, no borders, Accept/Reject vocabulary. Screenshot review with Ryan before shipping. Gherkin specs with the change, and a p.apyr.us docs task at the end.

Related: PPY-83e413 (CLI requires amplify_outputs.json), PPY-5a3624 (remote approval), PPY-7c458d (renewable sessions), PPY-06d692 (sign-in docs), PPY-e2a0b8 (enrollment).
